takeaway: The left pleura leaves the midline at the 4th costal cartilage to make room for the heart; the pleurae meet in the midline at the 2nd.

lines.text: The two pleural sacs meet in the midline, then part to make room for the heart. At which costal cartilage does the left one leave?
The pleurae start about 2.5 cm above the clavicle, at the border of its medial and middle thirds.
lines.say: The pleurae start about two and a half centimetres above the clavicle, at the border of its medial and middle thirds.

lines.text: They run obliquely down to meet in the midline at the 2nd costal cartilage.
lines.say: They run obliquely down to meet in the midline at the second costal cartilage.

lines.text: At the 4th costal cartilage, the left pleura leaves the midline.
lines.say: At the fourth costal cartilage, the left pleura leaves the midline.

lines.text: It swings out to make room for the heart.
So the answer is the 4th costal cartilage.
lines.say: (clears throat) So the answer is the fourth costal cartilage.
